title: Clark University (Clark)
summary: Clark University (Clark) is a university in Worcester. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with Clark.

sections.heading: What Clark is known for
paragraphs: Clark University is a private nonprofit institution known for its commitment to providing a focused and personalized undergraduate education. With an enrollment of 2,214 students, Clark offers a range of academic programs, including a notable business program that accounts for approximately 10.02% of its offerings. The university emphasizes a supportive learning environment, fostering close interactions between students and faculty. Clark's status as a private nonprofit college reflects its dedication to academic excellence and student development.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: Clark University is a private nonprofit institution that offers a diverse range of academic programs. While it does not have programs in health fields, approximately 3.13% of its academic offerings are in education. This focus reflects Clark's commitment to preparing students for careers in teaching and educational leadership. As a private nonprofit college, Clark emphasizes personalized education and close faculty-student engagement, supporting a collaborative and enriching academic environment.

sections.heading: Popular majors
paragraphs: Clark University offers a variety of academic programs, with business being one of the most popular majors, representing about 10.02% of its academic offerings. The university also provides programs in computer science, which account for approximately 4.18% of its curriculum. Education programs make up around 3.13%, while public administration comprises about 0.21% of the academic portfolio. Notably, Clark does not offer programs in health-related fields. These distributions highlight Clark's focus on business, education, and computer science within its diverse academic environment.

sections.heading: How to read Clark tuition
paragraphs: Clark University (Clark) charges a tuition fee of $58,867 for both in-state and out-of-state students. This uniform tuition rate means that residency status does not affect the tuition cost. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition along with additional expenses such as fees, room, board, and other related costs, amounts to $68,432. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and families anticipate the financial commitment required to attend Clark.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Clark University (Clark) offers financial aid opportunities to assist students in managing the cost of attendance. Approximately 23.13% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies awarded to undergraduate students demonstrating financial need. Among students who complete their programs, the median debt incurred is $26,759. Prospective students can explore detailed financial aid information and use the net price calculator available on Clark's official website at www.clarku.edu/ or through the College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?165334 to better understand potential costs and aid options.

paragraphs: Clark University does not have distinct colleges or schools within its academic structure. Instead, it offers a range of undergraduate and graduate programs through its centralized academic departments. This organizational approach allows for interdisciplinary collaboration and flexibility in course offerings, catering to diverse student interests and academic goals.

paragraphs: Clark University (Clark) offers degree programs at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. sections.heading: Housing and dining
paragraphs: Clark University (Clark) provides housing options for students both on and off campus, with the cost of room and board set at $12,500 regardless of the living arrangement. paragraphs: Clark University is located in Worcester, Massachusetts, within the zip code 01610. The Clark campus is integrated into the urban environment of Worcester, providing students with access to various city amenities and resources. sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Clark University (Clark) has a completion rate of approximately 76.94% within 150% of the normal time to graduate, reflecting the proportion of students who successfully finish their programs. Graduates of Clark experience median earnings of $49,022 six years after enrollment, which increase to $62,381 ten years after enrollment, indicating positive career progression over time. Among students who complete their degrees, the median debt incurred is $26,759, providing insight into the financial investment associated with earning a degree from Clark. These figures collectively illustrate the career outcomes and economic impact of a Clark education.

sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Clark University (Clark) demonstrates a diverse student body with women comprising approximately 56.55% and men about 43.45% of the enrollment. The racial and ethnic composition includes around 62.01% White students, 5.47% Black students, 13.01% Hispanic students, and 6.91% Asian students. Additionally, about 23.13% of students receive Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of the student population comes from lower-income backgrounds. This demographic distribution reflects Clark's commitment to fostering an inclusive and varied campus community.
